query: What drives customer satisfaction (Overall Rating) across the different airlines?

per_column.name: crew_professionalism_attentiveness
per_column.rationale: Service-quality dimension extracted from review text; plausibly drives satisfaction and is not a restatement of the rating itself.

per_column.name: service_personalization
per_column.rationale: A distinct experiential aspect of service; a legitimate external driver of overall satisfaction.

per_column.name: customer_support_quality
per_column.rationale: Support responsiveness is a plausible antecedent of satisfaction, separate from the outcome.

per_column.name: seat_physical_comfort_and_space
per_column.rationale: Physical comfort dimension; predictive of satisfaction. Overlaps with existing Seat Comfort column but is a legitimate driver, not a restatement of the rating.

per_column.name: food_and_beverage_quality
per_column.rationale: Meal quality is a genuine driver; overlaps with existing Food & Beverages column but not with the rating itself.

per_column.name: cabin_atmosphere_quality
per_column.rationale: Ambience dimension plausibly influencing satisfaction; external to the rating.

per_column.name: onboard_product_amenities
per_column.rationale: Amenity availability is a plausible external predictor of satisfaction.

per_column.name: operational_punctuality_reliability
per_column.rationale: Punctuality is a strong, well-known driver of airline satisfaction and is not captured in existing columns.

per_column.name: ground_and_airport_service_quality
per_column.rationale: Ground/airport experience is a distinct antecedent of overall satisfaction.

per_column.name: aircraft_cleanliness_and_maintenance
per_column.rationale: Cleanliness is a plausible driver of satisfaction, external to the outcome.

per_column.name: pricing_and_value_perception
per_column.rationale: Value perception drives satisfaction; overlaps with existing Value For Money but is a legitimate predictor rather than a restatement of the rating.

per_column.name: seat_class_expectation_consistency
per_column.rationale: Meeting expectations (e.g., downgrade surprise) is a plausible driver of dissatisfaction.

per_column.name: traveler_type_segment
per_column.rationale: Segment mediates expectations and satisfaction; a legitimate contextual predictor (though largely duplicates existing Type of Traveller).

per_column.name: route_distance_and_flight_duration
per_column.rationale: Haul length shapes expectations and experience; a plausible contextual predictor derivable from Route.

per_column.name: communication_clarity_and_information
per_column.rationale: Clarity of information is a plausible external driver of satisfaction, especially during disruptions.

per_column.name: policy_enforcement_consistency
per_column.rationale: Perceived fairness of policy enforcement plausibly influences satisfaction; external to the rating.

judge.rationale: All 16 columns are experiential/contextual dimensions extracted from review text (and route/traveler metadata) that lie outside the overall_rating and plausibly carry predictive signal about it. None restate the rating or constitute leakage (they are drivers/antecedents, not deterministic functions or post-outcome facts). As a set they cover a broad, semantically rich span of satisfaction drivers—crew, service, support, comfort, food, punctuality, ground service, cleanliness, value, expectations, communication, and fairness—giving strong predictive leverage. Utility is discounted slightly because several columns overlap with existing rating sub-scores (Seat Comfort, Food & Beverages, Value For Money) and metadata (Type of Traveller, Route), reducing incremental signal beyond the original columns, and because many are themselves derived from the same reviews that drive the rating, risking collinearity.
